nor_flintman.text: There's no good building stone in Norfolk, so we build with flint: hard nodules from the chalk, split open with a hammer to show the black glassy heart. That's knapping.
Squared flints laid with pale stone in patterns is called flushwork. Look at the church porches round here: chequerboards, stars, letters, all in flint. It's East Anglia's special trick.
Corners and windows we do in brick, mind. You can't make a sharp corner out of a pebble. Norfolk's tried for a thousand years.
